evidence_of_progress.note: Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 21.5% (104.1/484.4) vs 22.9% (102.3/447.6) in Q1 2025, from consensus actuals, matching CEO's 21.5% (doc 193272). Q2 2026 21.1%, about -300 bps per CFO, mostly $11.8M of restatement costs; excluding them, adjusted EBITDA rose 3.4% (doc 130231). FY2026 adjusted EBITDA guide $430M to $460M, trending to the low end, versus consensus $439M. Net leverage reached the 3.0x target a quarter early (8-K 2026-09-15).

verdict: Cheap and down, with an internal CEO and a new leverage and buyback framework, but no margin target; the -23% EBITDA revision (partly from car wash divestitures and restatement costs) puts this outside the GXO pattern.
open_questions: How much of the -23.5% FY2027 EBITDA revision is car wash deconsolidation versus true operating cuts? Pull consensus_history pid=4250 around the divestiture dates.
Will Rivera follow the leverage framework with a margin or EBITDA growth algorithm (for example, at an Investor Day) now that 3.0x is reached?
Are the material weaknesses and restatement (costs at the top of the $35M to $45M range) fully remediated, and does the securitization audit carry any risk?
